Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 1997 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

STARTER, SMITH PETERSON NAIL, 

ORTHOPAEDIC 



1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for Smith Peterson Nail Starter used in 
orthopaedic surgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 




ENLARGED 
SECTION YY 




DIA 10 



DlA 17 



HOLE, DIA 3 



ENLARGED 
SECTION XX 



SHARP 
EDGE 




All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 STARTER, SMITH PETERSON NAIL, ORTHOPAEDIC 

2.1 A deviation of ±2"5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 30CM3 of IS: 6603-1972 'Specification for 
stainless steel bars and flats '. 

4. Heat Treatment — The nail starter shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 450 to 
500 HV. 

5. Workmanship and Finish 

5.1 The starter shall be cannulated. 

5.2 The shape of the handle shall give a good grip. 

5.3 The edge of the tri-fln at the tip of the starter shall be sharp. 

5.4 The starter shall be free from cracks, draw-marks, burrs, surface contamination and impregnated 
foreign particles. 

5.5 The starter shall be clean, polished bright and passivated. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Performance — The starter shall be hammered to a thick piece of sheep or goat bone five times 
with a mallet. The edge of the starter shall not be damaged after the test.

6.2 Corrosion Resistance Test — Test the starter in accordance with IS: 7531-1975 'Method for 
boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments'. The 
starter shall show no sign of corrosion after the test. 



7. Marking — The starter shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized 




8. Packing —As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



Printed at Neelkamal Printers, Delhi, India
